Series::mvlgamma¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::mvlgamma(std::int64_t p) const
Series& Series::mvlgamma_(std::int64_t p)
Series& Series::mvlgamma_(std::int64_t p) const

What It Does¶

Computes the natural log of the multivariate gamma function of dimension p, elementwise. The multivariate gamma Gamma_p is the normalizing constant that shows up whenever a density is defined over p x p positive-definite matrices — the Wishart and inverse-Wishart distributions, the matrix-variate t, the marginal likelihood of a Gaussian with a conjugate covariance prior. It factors into ordinary gamma functions:

Gamma_p(x) = pi^(p(p-1)/4) * prod_{j=1..p} Gamma( x + (1 - j)/2 )

and mvlgamma() returns the log of that:

mvlgamma(x, p) = (p(p-1)/4) * ln(pi) + sum_{j=1..p} lgamma( x + (1 - j)/2 )

Working in log space is the point, for the same reason it is with lgamma: the individual gamma factors overflow quickly, while their logs stay in range and the product becomes a sum.

The parameter p changes the function being evaluated; it is not an axis and does not refer to the rank of self. A vector of candidate scalar arguments remains a vector after mvlgamma(3). The 3 says that each candidate is being used in a three-dimensional matrix normalizer.

Anchor facts:

  • mvlgamma(x, 1) = lgamma(x) exactly — the sum has a single term and the pi prefactor is pi^0 = 1.

  • The argument must satisfy x > (p - 1)/2, so that every gamma factor x + (1 - j)/2 has a positive argument. Outside that half-line mvlgamma() returns NaN.

mvlgamma() is out-of-place; mvlgamma_() overwrites the current storage.

Parameters¶

p (std::int64_t): the matrix dimension. Must be >= 1.

Returns¶

Series or Series& A Series with the same shape as self, each element replaced by mvlgamma(x, p), or NaN where x <= (p - 1)/2. mvlgamma_() returns a reference to the mutated series.

An integral input is promoted to float64.

Gradient¶

mvlgamma(., p) is differentiable with respect to x. Differentiating the sum term by term gives a sum of digamma values:

d/dx mvlgamma(x, p) = sum_{j=1..p} psi( x + (1 - j)/2 )

For p = 1 that is just psi(x), matching lgamma. p is a structural argument and carries no gradient. Where the forward value is NaN (outside the domain) the sensitivity is NaN too.

In-Place Form¶

mvlgamma_() is the in-place sibling of mvlgamma(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — mvlgamma_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
x.mvlgamma_(1);
std::cout << x;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0, 0.69314718]

Examples¶

Example 1. p = 1 reproduces lgamma.

pluss::series::print(std::cout,
                     pluss::make_series({2.0, 3.0, 4.0}).mvlgamma(1)) << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout,
                     pluss::make_series({2.0, 3.0, 4.0}).lgamma()) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 0.6931, 1.7918]
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 0.6931, 1.7918]

Example 2. Hold the candidate arguments fixed and change p. This isolates what the dimension parameter contributes: more shifted gamma terms and a larger pi prefactor, but no change to the shape of the returned series.

auto x = pluss::make_series({3.0, 4.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.mvlgamma(1)) << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.mvlgamma(2)) << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.mvlgamma(3)) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[0.6931, 1.7918]
Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1.5502, 3.5651]
Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[2.6949, 5.4030]

Example 3. The domain is x > (p - 1)/2. For p = 2 that means x > 0.5; 0.4 and 0.5 fall outside and come back NaN.

pluss::series::print(std::cout,
                     pluss::make_series({0.5, 0.6, 1.0}).mvlgamma(2)) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[nan, 3.2233, 1.1447]

Example 4. The backward pass is a sum of digamma terms.

auto x = pluss::make_series({3.0, 4.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
x.mvlgamma(2).sum().reverse();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity()) << "\n";

auto y = pluss::make_series({3.0, 4.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout,
                     y.digamma().add(y.sub(0.5).digamma())) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1.6259, 2.3593]
Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1.6259, 2.3593]

The sensitivity for p = 2 is psi(x) + psi(x - 0.5), reproduced on the right.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • p must be >= 1. p = 0 or a negative dimension raises mvlgamma: p must be >= 1.

  • The domain shrinks as p grows: x must exceed (p - 1)/2. Values on or below that bound return NaN, they do not raise.

  • mvlgamma(x, p) is not p * lgamma(x); the gamma arguments are shifted by half-integers and there is a pi prefactor.

  • p is not inferred from self.shape() and does not select a dimension of the series. Pass the matrix dimension represented by your statistical model.

  • p carries no gradient; only x does.

  • Out-of-place calls promote integral input to float64. The in-place form requires floating storage because it cannot write fractional results back into an integral buffer.

Summary¶

mvlgamma(x, p) is ln Gamma_p(x), the log multivariate gamma:

  • (p(p-1)/4) ln(pi) + sum_{j=1..p} lgamma(x + (1 - j)/2)

  • mvlgamma(x, 1) equals lgamma(x)

  • defined for x > (p - 1)/2; NaN outside

  • differentiable in x with backward sum_{j} psi(x + (1 - j)/2)

  • mvlgamma_() is the in-place form
